candidates.label: Gethsemane
candidates.support: Wikidata's coordinate for the traditional garden is corroborated by OpenBible.info's independently recorded point for the same site, at the foot of the Mount of Olives across the Kidron Valley from the Temple Mount. The general area is not disputed, but the exact garden plot is: at least two distinct denominational traditions claim the site, about 200 meters apart, including a Franciscan-custodied garden by the Church of All Nations and a Russian Orthodox garden near the Church of Mary Magdalene, and no first-century boundary of 'the garden' itself is archaeologically fixed.

summary.text: Gethsemane is a garden at the foot of the Mount of Olives, across the Kidron Valley from Jerusalem's Temple Mount and within an easy walk of the city. Its name comes from an Aramaic or Hebrew phrase, gat shemanim, for an olive-oil press, which fits its traditional identification as a working olive grove rather than an ornamental garden; terracing hillsides for cultivation was standard practice in this hill country, so the plot was likely terraced like its neighbors on the Mount of Olives.

history.text: According to Matthew and Mark, Jesus came to Gethsemane with his disciples on the night of his arrest and told them to sit while he went a little farther to pray; he returned twice, then a third time, to find them asleep. John, without naming the garden, places the same night's prayer in "a garden" beyond the brook Kidron, and says the party that arrested Jesus there was a detachment of soldiers with officers from the chief priests and the Pharisees, carrying lanterns, torches and weapons.

The exact plot the Gospels describe is not fixed: two Christian traditions a short walk apart both claim the site, including a Franciscan-custodied garden by the Church of All Nations and a Russian Orthodox garden near the Church of Mary Magdalene, and no first-century boundary of "the garden" is archaeologically established. The Franciscan garden, in Franciscan hands since 1681, holds eight of the oldest olive trees in the region, but a radiocarbon study found that the three datable trees all began growing in the twelfth century and share identical DNA, meaning today's trees descend from one parent planted long after the Gospel events rather than standing witnesses to them.

scripture.textWEB: Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane, and said to his disciples, “Sit here, while I go there and pray.”
They came to a place which was named Gethsemane. He said to his disciples, “Sit here while I pray.”

He came and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “Simon, are you sleeping? Couldn’t you watch one hour? Watch and pray, that you may not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.” Again he went away and prayed, saying the same words. Again he returned and found them sleeping, for their eyes were very heavy; and they didn’t know what to answer him. He came the third time and said to them, “Sleep on now, and take your rest. It is enough. The hour has come. Behold, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
When Jesus had spoken these words, he went out with his disciples over the brook Kidron, where there was a garden, into which he and his disciples entered.
Judas then, having taken a detachment of soldiers and officers from the chief priests and the Pharisees, came there with lanterns, torches, and weapons.
